newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech minister to announce Norway gas deal Wed.
newsitem.headline: Czech minister to announce Norway gas deal Wed.

text.p: Czech Minister of Trade and Industry Vladimir Dlouhy said on Tuesday that he expected to announce a positive end to talks over a long-term supply deal for Norway to supply natural gas to the Czech Republic.

"I expect that during my speech (on Wednesday)...I will be able in the presence of King Harald (of Norway) to announce the final results of these negotiations," Dlouhy told a news conference. Asked whether the results would be positive, he replied "yes".
A Norwegian industry ministry delegation accompanying Norway's King Harald on a state visit arrived in Prague on Tuesday. Oslo's Industrial Affairs Minister Grete Knudsen met Dlouhy around midday.
"We are very eager to sell Norwegian natural gas to the Czech Republic, because we have much unsold gas, and we can promise it on a long-term basis," Knudsen told the joint news conference.
Dlouhy declined to comment on the price or details of the supply, saying talks were still underway.
Dlouhy said last week that Norway had been given priority out of four options for natural gas supplies in the Czechs' effort to diversify away from solely Russian gas.

Earlier, the head of the gas industry division at Dlouhy's ministry said he thought the full Czech cabinet would probably decide on its final approval for the package with Norway next week. Dlouhy said he agreed with this.

The official, Oldrich Petrzilka, said the contract under negotiation was for three billion cubic metres per year for 15 years, with the option of extension to 20 years. He declined to give further details.
The other options included potential deals with German, Dutch and British suppliers or a second delivery route of Russian gas.
